weights.score_scale: 0-100 percentile ranks over valid cells per criterion; ties use average ranks; hard vetoes restrict new candidate selection
weights.bias_fix: Dust and storm remain soft scored criteria with lower within-climate weights; terrain, climate, solar, protection and science groups have equal weight.

vetoes.source: Bussey & Davis, NASA HEOMD/SMD Human Landing Sites Study (2015), Second Announcement, p. 3, https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/hls2-2nd-announcement-7-8.pdf
Bussey & Davis, NASA HEOMD/SMD Human Landing Sites Study (2015), Second Announcement, p. 3; MOLA is the stated datum. https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/hls2-2nd-announcement-7-8.pdf

vetoes.rule: approximately 25 km2 with slopes < approximately 10 degrees; screened as a 2x2-cell patch at 0.0625 degree resolution
vetoes.source: Bussey & Davis, NASA HEOMD/SMD Human Landing Sites Study (2015), Second Announcement, p. 3, https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/hls2-2nd-announcement-7-8.pdf
vetoes.notes: Water and habitat distances are scored resource/ISRU criteria, not vetoes. Raw material <3 km from the ISRU plant is from Bussey & Hoffman (2016), p. 16, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20160001040; infrastructure <5 km from the landing site is from the Second Announcement, p. 4, and Bussey & Hoffman (2016), p. 17.

resource_scoring_notes: Water distance and habitat feasibility remain scored evidence per Bussey & Hoffman (2016), pp. 16-17, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20160001040. Habitat flat-area distance is 0 km when the qualifying patch includes the landing cell; the patch's approximate area is also recorded.

validation.population: 2015 zone2015 locations vs all hard-veto-passing scored cells
